citation.source: Commonly cited culinary conversion: 1 pinch ≈ 1/16 tsp of fine table salt
citation.note: Same imprecise-by-convention figure tortilla-de-patatas.json's own identical salt instance already uses.

metadata.notes: The onion variant tortilla-de-patatas.json's own metadata named as a real gap ('Onion-free (sin cebolla) — no onion entity exists in this vocabulary yet'), now closed 2026-08-16. WASH/PEEL/CUT the potato AND separately PEEL/CUT the onion (both sliced); COMBINE_POTATO_ONION merges the two RAW sliced instances into one potato_onion_mixture (real technique: cooked together from raw, not fried separately then merged — see that action's own sequencingNote); FRY the joint mixture once (low heat, long duration, confit-style — 1500s, longer than the onion-free recipe's 900s potato-only fry, since a real potato+onion confit genuinely takes longer, both softening together); CRACK/BEAT/SALT the egg exactly as in the plain recipe; COMBINE_CON_CEBOLLA merges the fried mixture with beaten egg into tortilla_mixture_con_cebolla; FRY/FLIP/FRY as in the plain recipe.
metadata.instanceIdNote: targetInstanceId 'potato_onion_mixture-3'/'egg_shell-4'(unused directly)/'egg_cracked-5'/'tortilla_mixture_con_cebolla-6' are runtime-spawned ids (recipe-runner.ts's global spawnCounter, incremented once per spawn event across the WHOLE recipe, not per entity type) — hand-derived by walking the sequence in order: peel(potato) spawns potato_peel-1, peel(onion) spawns onion_peel-2, combine_potato_onion spawns potato_onion_mixture-3, crack(egg) spawns egg_shell-4 then egg_cracked-5, combine_con_cebolla spawns tortilla_mixture_con_cebolla-6. Verified by actually running this recipe through npm run validate's real end-to-end simulation (recipe-runner.ts's runRecipe), not just asserted — see tortilla-de-patatas.json's own identically-shaped note for why spawned ids can't be verified statically.
metadata.durationNote: The joint potato+onion fry's 1500s (25 minutes) sits within data/actions/fry.json's own wide 10s-1800s range and is longer than the plain recipe's potato-only 900s — a real, deliberate difference: onion releases significant water as it cooks down, and a genuine potato-and-onion confit for tortilla typically runs longer than potato alone to let both soften fully without either burning, consistent with caramelize.json's own 900-2700s citation for onion specifically (this step doesn't reach full caramelization — deep golden, not jammy-brown — but shares the same slow, patient low-heat logic).
